evidence.quote: In contrast, the approach struggles with the 81 multi-line and multi-file bugs, where it finds only 4 correct fixes.

Defects4J has at least one failing test case for each bug, which may not be the case for real-world usage scenarios. It will be interesting to evaluate RepairAgent on bugs with no a-priori available error-revealing test cases in future work.
Non-deterministic output of LLMs: The inherently non-deterministic nature of LLMs may result in different outcomes between two consecutive runs of RepairAgent.
Data leakage: GPT-3.5 may have seen parts of the Java projects we evaluate on during training.
Fault localization: Inaccurate or imprecise fault localization could lead to suboptimal repair suggestions or incorrect diagnoses.
Interacting with the LLM imposes an average cost of 270,000 tokens per bug, which, under the current pricing of OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 model, translates to 14 cents per bug.
For multi-line, multi-file bugs, we observe that RepairAgent often edits only a subset of the required locations.
